para.verbatim:
embed:rst Whether the ``.ini`` file carries anything to remap. ``false`` for a file that only WATCHES the character -- eg. a help overlay whose one section matches the position hash to know she is on screen, which remapped like a mod would draw a second copy of her :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` **Default**: ``true``

para.verbatim:
embed:rst Whether the ``.ini`` file is a RECOLOUR and nothing else: it draws none of the character's mesh, no other ``.ini`` file beside it does, and it overrides a texture of the character that the target does not draw. Its whole model then comes from downloads, with the mod's textures bound in place of the downloaded ones -- so a fixer that reads the mod's buffers while it is being built has to fetch those downloads first :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` **Default**: ``false``

briefdescription.para: Sets isRecolourOnly.

parameterdescription.para: Whether the file is a recolour and nothing else

para.verbatim:
embed:rst `Sections`_ a fix writes into every ``.ini`` file it generates, so a SIBLING's toggle keeps working there: a ``[Constants]`` declaring a copy of each variable a carried recolour's condition reads, and a copy of each sibling ``[Key...]`` section that cycles one, both under the copy's name :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` A file with no ``namespace =`` is named after its PATH, so a variable of one ``.ini`` cannot be read from another. The copy is driven by the same key under the same condition, so the two keep in step :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` **Default**: empty -- nothing to carry

para.verbatim: embed:rst Whether the mod leaves a mod object UNDRAWN -- on its own character the game never draws it, so a fix must not draw a download of it over the mod's own buffers

Asking for them runs the steps deferred to the first ask, like every other read of this data

embed:rst The rows of the :cpp:class:`GraphCollect` named 'name' among the parser's :cpp:member:`GIMIParser::commandEdits`, in the order it collected them: the variable of that name (see #variables). Empty for a name nothing filed, or a variable holding another type
.. warning:: The rows describe the graphs as they were when the collect ran (see :cpp:class:`GraphCollect`). A collect among deferred :cpp:member:`GIMIParser::commandEdits` runs on the FIRST ask of this data, so that first ask has to come before any edit to the graphs it reads: a fixer asks in its constructor, before its edits run. Asked first after an edit, the rows are read from the edited graphs

` :raw-html:`
` Which of several values a toggle shows before anyone presses a key is the one whose condition can hold together with this (:cpp:func:`GraphCollect::valueUnder`). A variable another file declares is left free

embed:rst Reads the mod's resource data off collected rows: each resource's file (#resourceFiles), and for each object its numbered draws (#drawRanges) and the parts they sit in (#drawParts), the texture registers it binds only after it has drawn (#lateBindings, unless #replacesTexturesByHash), the libraries it names (#libraries), the texture resources it binds only under a toggle (#toggledBindings), and whether it is hidden -- its `sections`_ draw nothing and skip the game's draw (#isUndrawn). Given :cpp:member:`ResourceDataRules::sections`, also every ``this =`` override (#thisOverrideOf, #isThisBound). Only the rows in an object's own root `sections`_ count, except that a draw or a ``run =`` anywhere it reaches counts as drawing :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` Given :cpp:member:`ResourceDataRules::toggles`, also the toggles that choose among the mod's textures: * **a ``this =`` toggle** (#thisToggleOf): a texture override binding several resources on its branches, or ONE under a condition that is not in :cpp:member:`ResourceDataRules::notToggles` (off, the original draws with the game's texture). When two `sections`_ bind one resource, the one that declares more of its own variants as `sections`_ keeps it * **a register toggle** (#registerToggleOf): a texture override binding one texture register to several resources on its branches, per `section`_ and register

parameterdescription.para: The variables it reads: the rows of each collect 'rules' names, by its name (see variables)
What it adds to eg. replacesTexturesByHash, which decides lateBindings

simplesect.para: The resource data, which the getters above read from the variable ResourceDataVar

para.verbatim:
embed:rst Reads which file each mod object takes for each texture role: #textureRoles, #roleCandidates, #rejections, #roleFile, and each texture resource's file (#rolesOfResource, #resourceOfFile) :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` A file is a candidate for a role when the ``.ini`` states it: a texture override's own ``hash =`` names a game texture of the role, an object's `section`_ binds it at a register of the role, a linked ``.ini`` recolours that texture or binds it on the same draw, or -- for a ``.dds`` nothing states -- its pixels are the game texture's (:cpp:member:`RoleFileRules::identify`). A file the folder does not hold, or one a previous fix wrote (``RemapDL`` / ``RemapTex``), is none. A flat file, or one an object binds for a second role too, is refused for a region role (:cpp:member:`RoleFileRules::regionRoles`) :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` Each object then takes, in this order: #. a file not declared by its hash as ANOTHER role #. the file bound only on this object, then on it and others, then on none, then only on others #. a file declared by its hash, then one bound at a register, then one known by its pixels #. of two hashes of one role, the newest (:cpp:member:`RoleFileRules::hashAge`) #. of two `sections`_ of one hash, the one 3DMigoto applies last: the higher ``match_priority``, then the `section`_ name later in order #. the file whose resource is declared first -- reported as a tie (:cpp:member:`RoleFile::tiedFile`) The variants of one toggle are not ranked against each other: the toggle's first-named variant among the candidates is chosen, and all of them recorded (:cpp:member:`RoleFile::variants`). A toggle is a ``this =`` or register toggle (#thisToggleOf, #registerToggleOf), or one register an object's graph -- through ``run =``, or in a linked ``.ini`` -- binds to several resources under conditions
embed:rst The variables it reads: the rows of each collect 'rules' names, by its name, and the #ResourceData under #ResourceDataVar (its toggles and resource files)

simplesect.para: What it chose, which the getters above read from the variable RoleFilesVar

para.verbatim:
embed:rst What a parser learned about a ``.ini`` file that a fixer needs and cannot read off the sections it is handed -- the classification data a parser keeps, whatever the game :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` Every :cpp:class:`BaseIniParser` owns one (:cpp:func:`BaseIniParser::parseData`): the parser fills it while it parses, and a fixer reads it through the parser it is given. A parser that fills nothing leaves the defaults, which say "everything is there": the file has something to remap, no mod object is undrawn, and no texture has a known role :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` A mod object is ``(component, object)``, as the parser's graphs are keyed -- eg. ``("Body", "C")`` for a slot of a GI component, ``("", "component3")`` for a Wuthering Waves draw slot :raw-html:`
` :raw-html:`
` What the mod's textures ARE comes in three layers, each read off the one before: which roles each file plays (#textureRoles), the candidates left for each role once the files that cannot serve it are refused (#roleCandidates, #rejections), and the one file each mod object takes for a role (#roleFile). The expensive ones may be filled on the first ask -- see #defer
